captures.title: New Vocational GCSEs unveiled in major shake-up to hands-on learning for teens
captures.date_review_note: Official Content API explicitly records first publication.
captures.rights: GOV.UK内容一般适用Open Government Licence v3.0，须署名，且不覆盖徽标、个人信息及第三方权利；当前候选须逐篇排除第三方引文和媒体后才能公开分发。
captures.text:
Every young person across the country will be able to pursue prestigious new Vocational GCSEs and access work experience in a major shake-up of the education system to prepare them for the world of work.

Delivering on the Prime Minister’s commitment in his first week in the role to put technical education on an equal footing with the traditional academic path, the new national qualifications will be created to sit alongside traditional GCSEs and will replace the current Technical Awards.

Part of action to revolutionise technical and vocational learning, the rigorous new qualifications will help ensure today’s students have the skills for the jobs of the future.

The shake-up builds on reforms including new V Levels, Occupational and Foundation Certificates and expanded T Levels – giving young people more routes to a brighter future, ensuring they have a clear line of sight to employment, and helping to tackle the crisis of the 1 million young people who are out of education, employment or training.

Alongside revolutions inside the classroom, the government is launching a National Mission on Work Experience, working alongside the Good Growth Business Forum and other businesses, to boost opportunities outside the classroom.

It is a call to arms to employers to provide an additional 200,000 work experience placements to ensure all young people have vital exposure to the workplace between 14 and 16, with Mayors and local authorities helping to make links between schools and employers. This could include spending time in key sectors including accountancy firms, digital media companies and construction companies. Employers can contact their local Careers Hub to pledge new work experience placements.

Alongside businesses, No10 North will establish work experience placements for 14-16 year old students this academic year. This will give young people the chance to see into the heart of government, experience the world of work, and demonstrate the real opportunities available to them on their doorstep

It is part of the Prime Minister’s mission to fix the most difficult issues facing the country, and create opportunities in every postcode.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:

We’ve all heard someone say ‘school wasn’t really for me’ because they were not given the chance to study vocational courses as well as traditional subjects.

That one-size-fits-all approach isn’t working, so we’re building an education system that values both academic and technical paths.

I want to give all young people across Britain the hope that their future will be brighter - whether it starts at university or not.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell said:

Young people today are entering a world of work full of exciting opportunities. We need to prepare them for it. Time and again young people, parents and employers tell me they want schools to do more to help them understand and prepare for the jobs of the future.

That is why we are transforming technical education and ensuring every young person can access the knowledge, skills and experiences they need to thrive in a changing world.

Our new Vocational GCSEs will give young people a stronger connection to the careers and industries shaping our economy, helping them discover and develop their talents while maintaining high standards across our education system.

This is not about creating different routes for different children. It is about ensuring every child has access to a rich and ambitious education that opens doors, creates opportunity and prepares them for life beyond the classroom.

The same size as GCSEs, these new qualifications will be nationally set, with subject content based on subject expert advice. Assessment and grading will be regulated by Ofqual to ensure full parity with traditional GCSEs.

They will eventually replace existing Technical Awards, which currently vary by provider with no nationally set content, and do not consistently support progression to further study.

They are set to be available in some subjects from as early as September 2029, as part of broader new technical pathways starting in September 2028. Subject options could include Business Management and Finance, Creative Media Production, Digital Tech, Child Development, and Building and Construction, supporting progression into further study through T Levels and V Levels in these subjects, or through A Levels.

New subjects will be developed as part of a review of existing GCSEs and new Vocational GCSEs, to create a complementary set of qualifications that give students greater choice, but avoid duplication or unnecessary overlap. English, Maths and Science will remain a common entitlement. Together, the qualifications on offer at age 14 will be aligned to 16-19 progression routes including A Levels, T Levels and the new V Levels.

The work to move away from a one-size-fits-all system designed in Whitehall was kicked off earlier this month as the Education Secretary hosted a summit at No10 North with mayors, businesses, schools and colleges.

Sir Hamid Patel CBE, Chief Executive of Star Academies, said:

Over the past two decades, we have strengthened GCSEs through greater rigour, clearer and more coherently sequenced subject content, and more robust assessment. These reforms extend those same high standards into vocational education, ensuring qualifications are underpinned by nationally agreed content, strong regulatory oversight and clear progression routes into apprenticeships, T Levels, V Levels, A Levels, higher education and employment.

The new vocational GCSEs have the potential to command the confidence of parents, employers, colleges and universities alike, while providing young people with meaningful pathways into high-skilled careers. Importantly, they will sit alongside a strong core academic education, ensuring that pupils continue to study the essential subjects that underpin future success. Crucially, they can help ensure that education is better aligned to the skills and workforce needs of local communities and regional economies, supporting the growth ambitions of mayors and combined authorities across the country.

John Yarham, Chief Executive Officer, The Careers & Enterprise Company, said:

We welcome the national mission on work experience. High-quality pathways, alongside modern work experience, are vital to bringing the world of work to life and giving young people the skills and knowledge they need for their future.

Employers of all sizes and sectors tell us they see real benefits from outreach that builds diverse future talent. To make this happen at scale, we need an ambitious shared framework, underpinned by strong local coordination, so opportunities are targeted where they can have the greatest impact – particularly for young people currently missing out.

CEC stands ready to work with our Careers Hub partners in every region, connecting employers with schools and colleges to create more high-quality opportunities and bridge the gap between education and the world of work.

Michelle Ovens CBE, CEO & Founder of Small Business Britain, said:

We’re pleased to see the government’s mission to boost work experience opportunities for young people. Small businesses across the country are often where young people get their first exposure to the world of work, helping them build practical skills and experience, while also playing a vital role in strengthening local and regional economies.

Stronger public-private partnerships between government, education and business are vital to ensuring young people leave education with the skills, experience, and confidence they need to navigate the world of work, and that small businesses are equipped to help provide those opportunities.

Sarah Bradbury, Chief Executive of IGD, said:

Modern work experience has the power to open young people’s eyes to careers they may never have considered and give them the skills and confidence to take that first step into work. Through our industry-wide Feeding Britain’s Future movement, businesses within the food and drink industry are trialling a new, flexible approach in partnership with The Careers & Enterprise Company, that brings employers together to create meaningful work experiences at scale. The food and drink industry is the UK’s largest private sector employer and we want young people to see the huge range of opportunities it offers. We welcome the national mission on work experience and stand ready to work with industry to bridge the gap between schools, colleges and the world of work.

Shevaun Haviland CBE, Director General of the British Chambers of Commerce said:

Business leaders are deeply committed to their communities and want to support young people on their journey from education to employment.

That’s why the British Chambers of Commerce is pleased to support the National Mission on Work Experience, and will work through our Chambers, who are already closely engaged with both businesses and schools across the country, to rally local employers to the cause.

Expanding access to work experience and increased business engagement in schools is critical to supporting the workforce of tomorrow. It is welcome that this government initiative is being delivered in partnership with business organisations.

Irene Graham, CEO , ScaleUp Institute, said:

Scaling firms, across sectors and regions, are strong supporters of work experience. This National Mission is a vital one to help young people’s entry in to the world of the work and the ScaleUp Institute looks forward to supporting the initiative as it develops.

Rt Hon Robert Halfon, Executive Director of Made UK said:

Manufacturers and Make UK warmly welcome the National Mission on Work Experience and the Government’s commitment to expanding technical education. The Prime Minister is right that the gap between the classroom and the workplace has to be bridged if we are to equip young people with the skills employers need.

For too long, too many young people have left school without meaningful exposure to the world of work or a clear understanding of the opportunities available to them. Work experience and technical education can be transformative, helping young people develop confidence, build employability skills and gain the knowledge and practical experience that employers value.

This call on employers across the country to create more opportunities is an important step forward, but what matters now is quality. Delivering the right mix of technical knowledge and practical application, backed by qualifications employers recognise and close collaboration between industry and education, will ensure every young person has the chance to access a genuine ladder of opportunity into skilled, well-paid careers.

Rob Nitsch CEO Federation of Awarding Bodies said;

These developments are positive; it is absolutely right that the blend of classroom and practical learning should be extended, and that the focus is on better choices at 16. Awarding Organisations will also welcome the acknowledgement of the place of practical skills assessments in courses of learning that are practical in nature and will look forward to contributing to the development of the new pathways.

Alan Milburn’s interim report into NEETs commissioned by the government warned that Britain is at risk of a “lost generation”. His findings painted a stark picture of a system that too often leaves young people leaving school without the skills, experience or connections they need to step into the world of work.

He pointed to “strong evidence” that practical learning is effective in helping those at risk of being NEET move into work.

The White Working Class Inquiry also laid bare the lack of opportunity for working-class children to thrive, concluding that the technical and vocational system is broken for disadvantaged groups.

It highlighted that vocational and technical routes are valued highly by white working-class families, and recommend a major structural overhaul of technical and vocational routes to help close the disadvantage gap.

Notes to Editors

Local leaders, employers, schools and colleges will play a key role in deciding the subjects to reflect skills needs. A consultation will also be launched later in the year to help shape the new qualifications and get views from local leaders.

It comes on top of ambitious curriculum and GCSE reforms that will make sure schools are preparing youngsters to have the knowledge and skills needed to genuinely thrive in the workplace. As part of this, there will be a greater emphasis on practical skills and assessments in practical GCSE subjects such as PE , Drama, Design and Technology, Food and Nutrition, Music and Computing to properly recognise the value of these skills and further support students to succeed beyond the classroom.

The government will adapt school performance measures ensuring Ofsted and the accountability system support these new qualifications, so schools are appropriately incentivised to offer these valuable opportunities for young people.

16 year olds will be able to take the first V Levels in Education, Finance and Digital, from September 2027, alongside new T Levels in Sports, Fitness and Exercise Science, and Care Services from 2028. New Occupational and Further Study Pathways are also being introduced to help students progress onto A, V or T Levels, or into employment or an apprenticeship.

Work experience for 14 to 16 year olds is additional to the industry placements that students currently complete through T Levels.

captures.title: Government to act on Thirlwall patient safety recommendations
captures.date_review_note: Official Content API explicitly records first publication.
captures.rights: GOV.UK内容一般适用Open Government Licence v3.0，须署名，且不覆盖徽标、个人信息及第三方权利；当前候选须逐篇排除第三方引文和媒体后才能公开分发。
captures.text:
Government sets out immediate steps to strengthen patient safety and safeguarding following the Thirlwall Inquiry

Urgent work launched on neonatal ‘cot cams’ to improve safety and give reassurance to parents with babies in hospital

Action also includes tougher accountability for NHS managers, stronger inspections and safeguarding reforms

Comes as Health Secretary chairs first meeting as Chair of the Maternity and Neonatal Taskforce, established following the Amos and Ockenden maternity reviews

The Health and Social Care Secretary has set out immediate actions to strengthen patient safety, safeguarding and accountability across the NHS, following the publication of Lady Justice Thirlwall’s final report into the Countess of Chester Hospital .

The Thirlwall Inquiry found serious failures of governance, leadership and safeguarding, with opportunities missed to act on concerns and protect babies from harm.

Responding to the findings in Parliament, the Health and Social Care Secretary said safeguarding must be at the heart of the NHS and that the government would act on the inquiry’s recommendations to help prevent such failures happening again.

Health and Social Care Secretary Yvette Cooper said:

The suffering endured by these babies and their families is impossible to comprehend.

On behalf of the government and the health service, I am profoundly sorry for the failures set out so clearly in this report.

For the harm, distress and unthinkable loss for their families. For the failures by the NHS to keep babies safe.

The government has begun work on a series of measures while it considers the inquiry’s recommendations in full, including:

urgent work to develop plans for CCTV, including ‘cot cams’, in neonatal settings to improve safety and provide reassurance to parents

new guidance on the safe use and storage of insulin and strengthened guidance for medical examiners reviewing neonatal deaths

plans to regulate NHS managers through a barring scheme for senior leaders who fail in their responsibilities

continued rollout of the National Bereavement Care Pathway for families experiencing neonatal loss, with all NHS trusts now signed up to implement it

creation of a single tracker to monitor delivery of recommendations from major maternity and neonatal reviews and inquiries, helping ensure reforms are implemented and progress is transparent

In Parliament, the Health and Social Care Secretary said:

The safety and care for babies, the safeguarding of every patient, the respect for families - all these go right to the heart of our NHS values.

The inquiry recognises that in many areas things have changed since these terrible events took place, including welcome improvements at the Countess in services for women and children.

However, the inquiry is clear that new action is needed.

I take these recommendations extremely seriously and the government will of course consider the entire report and set out a full response.

Safeguarding is everyone’s business, and safeguarding must be everyone’s priority. Concerns must be heard and acted upon. Staff who speak up must be protected and taken seriously, and I expect every leader, every board across the NHS, every professional and manager, every member of staff to uphold their safeguarding responsibilities.

The Secretary of State also announced that safeguarding will be placed at the centre of the forthcoming Babies, Children and Young People’s Modern Service Framework, underlining the government’s commitment to making the safety of babies and children a core priority across the health service.

It comes as the Health and Social Care Secretary chaired her first meeting as Chair of the Maternity and Neonatal Taskforce this afternoon. The taskforce will translate the recommendations from the Ockenden and Amos reviews into an action plan for transforming care, to be published this year.

The government will publish its full response to Lady Justice Thirlwall’s recommendations once it has completed detailed consideration of the report.

captures.title: Pathway to stronger public control of the water industry revealed
captures.date_review_note: Official Content API explicitly records first publication.
captures.rights: GOV.UK内容一般适用Open Government Licence v3.0，须署名，且不覆盖徽标、个人信息及第三方权利；当前候选须逐篇排除第三方引文和媒体后才能公开分发。
captures.text:
The Prime Minister announced today (29 September) that the strengthened Water Bill will remove the current limits on government ownership of shares in the major water and sewerage companies in England.

Public interest should be at the heart of how our critical services operate. The Government intends to increase public control to deliver cleaner waters, fairer bills, stronger accountability and better outcomes for customers and the environment.

This change will remove a historic restriction on government share ownership, which does not exist in other sectors, so government can act where water companies let down customers and the environment.

Current limits set out in the Water Act 1989 on government ownership of shares in the major water and sewerage companies, and the associated restriction on government acquiring shares in those companies, will be removed. These limits vary between 1-3%, the exact limit varies by company and is below 3% in each case.

The change will apply in England.

The Government recognises that securing the long-term future of England’s water sector relies on continued private sector investment. Removing the cap does not change that. We will continue to work with investors, regulators and companies to secure the best outcomes for consumers and the environment.

This announcement gives the Government flexibility to consider a wide range of possible future interventions, including on ownership models, and provide support where it is needed. We are committed to delivering these reforms within the fiscal rules – which the Chancellor and Prime Minister have been clear will be met at Budget, with a buffer against uncertainty.

The Prime Minister also recognised that mayors and strategic authorities currently have far too little influence over companies’ priorities or mechanisms to hold them to account. New powers for local leaders will be developed as part of the Government’s reforms of the water sector.

Further details on the Government’s approach to the water industry will be set out in the 10-year plan for Britain, to be published later this year. This will set out plans for stronger public control over essentials like water, making them work for people and places again and will underpin the reform we will take forward through a strengthened Water Bill.

Public interest should be at the heart of how our critical services operate. The Government intends to increase public control to deliver cleaner waters, fairer bills, stronger accountability and better outcomes for customers and the environment.

This change will remove a historic restriction on government share ownership, which does not exist in other sectors, so government can act where water companies let down customers and the environment.

Current limits set out in the Water Act 1989 on government ownership of shares in the major water and sewerage companies, and the associated restriction on government acquiring shares in those companies, will be removed. These limits vary between 1-3%, the exact limit varies by company and is below 3% in each case.
The change will apply in England.

The Government recognises that securing the long-term future of England’s water sector relies on continued private sector investment. Removing the cap does not change that. We will continue to work with investors, regulators and companies to secure the best outcomes for consumers and the environment.

This announcement gives the Government flexibility to consider a wide range of possible future interventions, including on ownership models, and provide support where it is needed. We are committed to delivering these reforms within the fiscal rules – which the Chancellor and Prime Minister have been clear will be met at Budget, with a buffer against uncertainty.

The Prime Minister also recognised that mayors and strategic authorities currently have far too little influence over companies’ priorities or mechanisms to hold them to account. New powers for local leaders will be developed as part of the Government’s reforms of the water sector.

Further details on the Government’s approach to the water industry will be set out in the 10-year plan for Britain, to be published later this year. This will set out plans for stronger public control over essentials like water, making them work for people and places again and will underpin the reform we will take forward through a strengthened Water Bill.

captures.title: Government joins forces with Breast Cancer Now
captures.date_review_note: Official Content API explicitly records first publication.

captures.text:
Women to receive better support through their breast cancer journey with a new partnership to help them recognise possible signs of the disease earlier and access trusted post-treatment information and support

Action comes as new research from the UK’s largest breast cancer charity, Breast Cancer Now, reveals almost a third of women who check their breasts regularly do not feel confident about the signs of breast cancer to look out for

Partnership forms the first of those announced in the Renewed Women’s Health Strategy, to provide improved care for issues disproportionately affecting women

Women across the country will be better supported to spot the signs of breast cancer and know where to turn for help as the government today (5 October 2026) announces its first partnership to help deliver its Renewed Women’s Health Strategy .

Marking Breast Cancer Awareness Month, the Department of Health and Social Care will partner with the UK’s largest breast cancer charity, Breast Cancer Now, over the next 3 years, giving women practical information to build confidence in checking their breasts, recognising changes, and seeking advice sooner - particularly in underserved areas.

It comes as new research from Breast Cancer Now reveals almost a third (29%) of women in England who regularly check their breasts do not feel confident to notice a change, while just over one in 10 (11%) of those checking less than once a month say it’s because they do not know what to look out for.

One in 5 (20%) UK adults also say they are not confident they would know where to find trusted information about breast cancer if they had concerns.

Women will also be provided with better support after their treatment, including clear information to understand the possible signs of breast cancer returning or spreading and how to live a healthy lifestyle post breast cancer treatment.

Healthcare professionals will receive additional training, alongside a practical toolkit for healthcare teams, so they can provide the best possible advice to women adapting post-treatment.

Minister for Women’s Health and Maternity, Baroness Merron, said:

Breast cancer survival rates have improved enormously thanks to advances in our understanding of, and ability to treat, this disease, but it is still the case that early diagnosis is vital for each individual’s chances of survival.

That’s why we need to ensure every woman feels confident checking their breasts, recognising the possible signs of the disease, and getting any new or unusual breast changes checked by a GP. The sooner breast cancer is diagnosed, the better the chances of successful treatment, and the more lives we will save.

As part of our Renewed Women’s Health Strategy, we’re joining forces with Breast Cancer Now to get trusted information directly to the women who need this support. That is exactly what the strategy set out to do - listening to women, meeting them where they are and helping them live healthier lives.

One in 7 women in the UK will be diagnosed with breast cancer during their lifetime and around 11,500 women still die from the disease each year. Caught early, at stage 1, almost 100% of people survive for at least 5 years. But when it’s caught late, at stage 4, that drops to 32%, making it cause for deep concern that so many women lack confidence in spotting breast cancer signs and symptoms.

Rachael Franklin, Deputy Chief Executive at Breast Cancer Now, said:

We’re hugely proud to be the first partner of the Renewed Women’s Health Strategy, working with the Department of Health and Social Care to deliver our shared ambition of supporting women to live healthy, fulfilling lives. Breast awareness and ensuring women know where to turn for support are crucial to achieving this.

By joining forces we’re driving progress faster and saving lives. We know early detection is vital, with almost 100% of people diagnosed at stage 1 surviving for 5 years or more, compared with just 32% at stage 4, when breast cancer has spread and become incurable.

Together, we’ll tackle the challenges in front of us and ensure all women are confident in checking their breasts and recognising changes, know where to turn to and get answers, throughout treatment and beyond, equipped with the vital information and support they need at every stage.

Better serving women means meeting them where they are, listening to what they need, and ensuring every woman gets the information and support to spot breast cancer sooner. From the first check to treatment and beyond, we’ll be there.

The partnership is the first to be announced as part of the government’s Renewed Women’s Health Strategy, which puts women’s voices at the heart of improving healthcare and sets out action to help women live healthier, more fulfilling lives.

The Department of Health and Social Care will partner with Breast Cancer Now to deliver 3 outcomes:

women can easily access trusted breast health information

women make regular breast checking a habit, recognise the signs and symptoms of breast cancer, and know to go straight to a GP if they notice any unusual changes

women are supported when finishing primary breast cancer treatment, with crucial information about spotting any signs of breast cancer returning

captures.title: Government acts to crack down on school uniform-rip offs
captures.date_review_note: Official Content API explicitly records first publication.
captures.rights: GOV.UK内容一般适用Open Government Licence v3.0，须署名，且不覆盖徽标、个人信息及第三方权利；当前候选须逐篇排除第三方引文和媒体后才能公开分发。
captures.text:
Families will no longer be at the mercy of rip-off uniform suppliers or schools dodging cost limits, as the government closes loopholes that have allowed some schools to sidestep limits on expensive branded items.

There will be no more hiding behind “optional” branded items with no cheap alternative, and no more pressuring parents into costly branded sports kit.

New rules – in force from this week – cap branded items at 3 for primary pupils and 4 for secondary . Schools will be told to work with suppliers that offer payment plans and run regular contract reviews, so families aren’t at the mercy of a single costly supplier.

It comes as nearly half of parents (47%) say uniform is their biggest back-to-school worry, as government ramps up cost of living support for families this month.

The changes sit within a broader support package launched this week:

free school meals are being extended to every child in a household receiving Universal Credit (3 million total), benefitting at least 500,000 more children and saving families £500 per child per year

eligible parents of children aged 9 months to school age can access the full 30-hour government-funded childcare hours a week from the start of the autumn term, saving up to £8,000 a year per child. This is alongside parents being able to access over 9000 childcare places from September 2026 through the school-based nursery programme

over 1,400 more schools will launch free breakfast clubs , taking the total to more than 2,700 clubs open nationwide benefiting over 680,000 children, saving families £450 and 95 hours a year

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:

The cost of sending your child to school has got out of hand, and parents are rightly fed up. School uniforms shouldn’t be charged at luxury prices when they’re everyday essentials. That’s not right.

I’ve listened to parents and alongside the cap on branded items that came in this week, I’m going further to change the rules. We’ll close loopholes and make sure schools shop around for suppliers and consider payment plans.

This is one of our everyday fixes to stop families paying over the odds, give them the breathing room they deserve and help to bring back hope across the country.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell said:

No family should be priced out by a school’s choice of uniform supplier or an insistence on branded items. We’ve been clear with schools - three items for primary, four for secondary, no exceptions and no excuses. If schools try to work around that, we will step in.

This is about real breathing space for families this school year, on top of the support we’re already delivering through free school meals, breakfast clubs and childcare.

Dan Paskins, Executive Director of UK Impact at Save the Children, said:

Parents have told us all summer about their worries about the cost of their children returning to school. Today’s announcement, alongside the new extension of free school meals and uniform grants, will remove some of that worry, and give families some breathing space to focus on supporting their children back to school.

Nearly half of all parents we polled said that school uniform costs were their primary financial concern around their children returning to school. The Prime Minister is right to go further to push schools to work with suppliers, recognising the pressure the cost of uniform has put parents under. Financial concerns should never impact a child’s education and these announcements will help ensure more children can focus on learning instead of being worried about food at school and having the right uniform.

Alongside the limits on branded items , guidance will be updated later this year on how schools buy uniform . Schools will be expected to seek out suppliers offering payment plans, and to review supplier arrangements at least every 5 years, so families are not left paying whatever one supplier chooses to charge.

The tightened guidance makes clear there are no excuses for schools dodging the limit - whether by listing an item as optional with no affordable alternative, or pressuring parents into costly branded sports kit.

The guidance follows research showing many parents are struggling with back to school costs. Nearly half (47%) rank uniform as their biggest financial worry, according to Save the Children, underlining why government says the cost of a school’s own choices should never fall unfairly on parents.

Processes are in place to ensure schools are following these rules correctly. If they fail to comply, the Education Secretary can take action to change a schools’ uniform policy where necessary.

captures.title: Healthier school dinners as government delivers major reforms
captures.date_review_note: Official Content API explicitly records first publication.
captures.rights: GOV.UK内容一般适用Open Government Licence v3.0，须署名，且不覆盖徽标、个人信息及第三方权利；当前候选须逐篇排除第三方引文和媒体后才能公开分发。
captures.text:
Healthier, tastier school dinners will be on the menu for millions of children across the country as the government delivers the biggest overhaul of school food in a generation.

The changes to the school food standards will see more fresh fruit and vegetables, fibre-rich foods and nutritious balanced meals that help children stay focused, energised and ready to learn throughout the school day.

The standards have been rigorously tested with schools, caterers and sample menus to make sure schools across the country will be able to provide exciting, healthy and nutritious meals that kids enjoy - from sweet chilli stir fry, to lasagne, to chicken or veg curries.

The school food revolution follows major reforms to give families breathing space with the cost of living, including a cap on the number of branded school uniform items. Three million children from families receiving Universal Credit are now eligible for free school meals and thousands of free breakfast clubs are operating across the country, thanks to government action.

Developed alongside nutritionists and public health experts, the new school food standards are backed by campaigners, charities and nutritional experts, including Chef Jamie Oliver and Dame Emma Thompson.

While many schools are already leading the way with excellent food, these reforms will ensure every child, wherever they live, benefit from the same high standards.

Education Secretary, Lucy Powell, said:

These are once-in-a-generation changes that will transform school food for children across the country.

From our historic expansion of free school meals to the rollout of free breakfast clubs and new school food standards, we are making sure that every child has access to the healthy meals we know children need to learn, grow and succeed.

No child should spend the school day hungry, and no family should have to struggle to put food on the table. This is what change looks like: healthier food, fuller stomachs and a fairer start for every child.

With one in three children leaving primary school overweight or obese, and tooth decay linked to high-sugar diets remaining the leading cause of hospital admissions among children aged five to nine, the case for change is clear. When asked what they would change to school dinners, parents called for the same changes we are making - with 36% wanting more fruit and vegetables in school meals, 38% wanting limits on fatty foods and 33% wanting less sugary food and drink.

Jamie Oliver, Chef and Child Health Campaigner, said:

Back 20+ years ago when I started School Dinners I could not believe that we had standards for dog food but not what we serve our children at school! And I’ve never stopped banging that drum. Because it’s massive - 190 days of the year 70% of our kids’ nutrition is in the hands of their school. So, it’s got to be great. It’s got to fill them up with all the good stuff they need to learn and grow.

So, it’s brilliant to see new School Food Standards based on the latest science, to make sure the food children get at school is actually supporting their health and helping them thrive. And, that those standards won’t just live on paper, but have proper monitoring to make sure they’re followed, so we know where we need to deploy care, love and support.

Sure, there’s always more to do, but after 25 years of campaigning, today is a brilliant day.

Dame Emma Thompson, Actor and Food Foundation Celebrity Ambassador, said:

For years, campaigners, parents and experts have called for school food standards to be updated, so I am thrilled to see this moment finally arrive.

Every child deserves access to healthy, nutritious food at school. Good food helps children learn, grow and flourish, and these new standards have the power to make a real difference to children across the country.

This is a milestone worth celebrating and an investment in a healthier future for the next generation.

Sarah Orves, Headteacher of Ilketshall Lawrence Primary in Suffolk, said:

Lunchtimes used to be just a moment to refuel and get back to the day, but it was our pupils themselves who told us they wanted change.

We started the journey of transforming our school food a year ago, introducing ‘Try it Tuesday’ and family taster sessions to bring both children and families on board, and now lunchtimes are something the kids genuinely feel excited about.

We’re only halfway through that journey, but we’re already noticing the difference: children are more social and settled at lunch, more focused in class, and genuinely excited to try new foods and engage with being healthy.

To give parents greater confidence in school meals, schools will be expected to publish their food policies and menus online and nominate a school food governor, helping parents, pupils and communities understand and hold schools to account for the food on offer.

To help schools implement the new standards, the government will provide training, resources and guidance. The Department for Education will work with the Food Standards Agency on an approach to monitoring school food, with more details in the coming months.

Alongside the historic expansion of free school meals and the rollout of free breakfast clubs, these changes represent the most significant package of school food improvements in a generation, giving parents confidence that their child is receiving healthy, nutritious food throughout the school day and helping children focus, learn and succeed at school.

Additional Quotes:

Anna Taylor, Executive Director, The Food Foundation, said:

Today marks another massive step on the journey to improve children’s health across the country. Good school food standards are critical to making that happen and the School Food Project is there to help schools train up their kitchen teams and work with pupils to improve menus. This all needs to be underpinned by a robust approach to monitoring and supporting schools to improve.

Over the coming year, in the run-up to enforcement in September 2027, parents and children can expect to start seeing real improvements.

Every child deserves the best possible start in life - and that means school food that packs a nutritional punch while bringing genuine pleasure and wellbeing to every child’s mealtime.

Bite Back campaigner, Zainab (19), said:

I was in Year 10 when I joined Bite Back, and since then I’ve campaigned alongside other young people for better school food. Bite Back exists to make sure young people are heard on decisions affecting our health, so it means a lot to see the Government listening.

Thousands of young people shared their experiences and ideas because we all want the same thing: great food in every school that helps children feel good, focus and thrive.

This announcement is an important step. We now look forward to working with the Government, schools and our partners to introduce the new standards successfully, monitor their impact and make sure they lead to real change in every school canteen.

Stephanie Slater MBE, founder and Chief Executive of School Food Matters, says:

We’re in schools every day and see the power of a nutritious school meal. We want to see delicious and nutritious meals in every school so today marks an important step towards equity in the school food system.

New standards and a framework for monitoring the quality of the food on offer will bring about the change we want to see: great school food that supports every child to thrive, wherever they live.

Naomi Duncan, CEO, Chefs in Schools, said:

Today is a huge day for children and young people. For far too long, excellent school kitchens serving fresh, tasty food have been competing with those serving up cheap, nutritionally barren junk. Today the government has drawn a line in the sand and committed to not just improving standards, but ensuring every single school kitchen is held to them.

We warmly welcome this action. History shows us that introducing higher standards leads in the long term to increasing uptake, when schools and caterers work together. Now the onus is on those of us who feed children every day in school to make sure that becomes reality again.

We’ve launched the School Food Project to support schools and caterers with implementation of these new ambitions, to protect and increase uptake and help to unleash the dynamism and creativity that we know exists in every school kitchen. We have a year to prepare and we shouldn’t waste a minute of it.

Charlotte Stirling-Reed -The Baby & Child Nutritionist:

I’ve been waiting a long time to see big changes happening once again with our school food.

It’s been over ten years since the School Food Standards were properly looked at, and in that time we’ve learned so much more about what children need to grow, develop and concentrate at school.

This feels as if it could be a pivotal moment for children’s health and I’m fully behind having clearer, more specific guidance around what foods should and shouldn’t be offered at school.

What I like most about these new school food recommendations is that the level of change being proposed seems just the right level - ambitious enough to make a real difference, but realistic enough for schools and caterers to actually put into practice with a little support.

With more children than ever now relying on free school meals, what’s served at school has never mattered more, and I really hope parents and schools get behind these changes and help push them forward, because the benefits will be felt by this generation of children and the ones who come after.

Professor Susan Jebb, Chair of the Food Standards Agency (FSA) said:

The FSA welcomes the Department for Education’s commitment in the 10-year health plan to update the School Food Standards, and we fully support the ambition to ensure children can access healthier food in schools.

We want to see school food standards that are effective in practice, and schools appropriately supported to meet them. That’s why we’ve been working closely with DfE, offering our expertise on food regulation, assurance and the practical considerations involved in implementation.

Our aim is to help shape a future approach that is practical, proportionate and deliverable, and we look forward to continuing to work with DfE to ensure every school is offering pupils food that meets the nutritional standards.

Dr Helen Stewart, Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health (RCPCH), Officer for Health Improvement said:

Childhood nutrition has never been more important. Our State of Child Health report highlights rising rates of childhood obesity, particularly among children in the most deprived communities, who are more likely to rely on school meals.

These changes are a welcome and long-overdue step towards ensuring all children have access to healthier food throughout the school day, helping to establish healthy habits that can last a lifetime. They also demonstrate the value of close collaboration between the health and education sectors in improving outcomes for children and giving every child the best possible start in life.

Katharine Jenner, Executive Director, Obesity Health Alliance said:

This is a major and very welcome step towards giving every child the best start in life. With one in three children leaving primary school above a healthy weight, we cannot afford to ignore the important role that school food plays in shaping children’s diets and long-term health.

Cutting back foods high in sugar, salt and saturated fat, while putting more fruit and vegetables on the menu, will help make the healthier choice the easier choice for millions of children.

Good school food will play an important role in achieving the government’s ambition to become a more preventative state. The next step is making sure these standards are properly implemented and monitored, so that every child benefits, regardless of where they live or their family’s income.

Brad Pearce, National Chair of The School Food People said:

The School Food People welcomes the Government’s continued ambition to improve children’s nutrition through revised School Food Standards. Our members and their dedicated frontline teams want to provide children and young people with nutritious, exciting and freshly prepared food that they genuinely want to eat every school day.

As the new standards roll out, it is vital that we protect the strength and sustainability of the school food sector that will be responsible for delivering them. That means realistic funding, a practical and fully supported implementation plan, investment in the workforce and kitchens, and sufficient time for caterers and suppliers to adapt and reformulate products where necessary.

We must also keep a close eye on meal uptake. New revised mandatory school food standards, while very much welcome, can only actually improve children’s diets if pupils continue to choose school meals. We are absolutely committed to working with Government, schools, families and the wider sector to make these changes a success.

Dr Oosh Devalia OBE, BSPD President said:

BSPD warmly welcomes the Government’s overhaul of school food. Tooth decay remains the most common reason for children aged five to nine to be admitted to hospital in England, usually to have decayed teeth removed under general anaesthetic. Sugar is the main driver of that decay, and it is also a key contributor to childhood obesity, so cutting it from school meals is a win for children’s overall health as well as their teeth.

For many children, particularly in our most deprived communities where decay rates are highest, a school lunch may be the main meal of their day. Getting it right matters. Tooth decay is almost entirely preventable, and every child deserves a healthy mouth.

The changes to the school food standards will see more fresh fruit and vegetables, fibre-rich foods and nutritious balanced meals that help children stay focused, energised and ready to learn throughout the school day.

The school food revolution follows major reforms to give families breathing space with the cost of living, including a cap on the number of branded school uniform items. Three million children from families receiving Universal Credit are now eligible for free school meals and thousands of free breakfast clubs are operating across the country, thanks to government action.

Developed alongside nutritionists and public health experts, the new school food standards are backed by campaigners, charities and nutritional experts, including Chef Jamie Oliver and Dame Emma Thompson.
While many schools are already leading the way with excellent food, these reforms will ensure every child, wherever they live, benefit from the same high standards.
Education Secretary, Lucy Powell, said:
These are once-in-a-generation changes that will transform school food for children across the country.

From our historic expansion of free school meals to the rollout of free breakfast clubs and new school food standards, we are making sure that every child has access to the healthy meals we know children need to learn, grow and succeed.

No child should spend the school day hungry, and no family should have to struggle to put food on the table. This is what change looks like: healthier food, fuller stomachs and a fairer start for every child.

With one in three children leaving primary school overweight or obese, and tooth decay linked to high-sugar diets remaining the leading cause of hospital admissions among children aged five to nine, the case for change is clear. When asked what they would change to school dinners, parents called for the same changes we are making - with 36% wanting more fruit and vegetables in school meals, 38% wanting limits on fatty foods and 33% wanting less sugary food and drink.
Jamie Oliver, Chef and Child Health Campaigner, said:

Back 20+ years ago when I started School Dinners I could not believe that we had standards for dog food but not what we serve our children at school! And I’ve never stopped banging that drum. Because it’s massive - 190 days of the year 70% of our kids’ nutrition is in the hands of their school. So, it’s got to be great. It’s got to fill them up with all the good stuff they need to learn and grow.

So, it’s brilliant to see new School Food Standards based on the latest science, to make sure the food children get at school is actually supporting their health and helping them thrive. And, that those standards won’t just live on paper, but have proper monitoring to make sure they’re followed, so we know where we need to deploy care, love and support.
Sure, there’s always more to do, but after 25 years of campaigning, today is a brilliant day.
Dame Emma Thompson, Actor and Food Foundation Celebrity Ambassador, said:
For years, campaigners, parents and experts have called for school food standards to be updated, so I am thrilled to see this moment finally arrive.

Every child deserves access to healthy, nutritious food at school. Good food helps children learn, grow and flourish, and these new standards have the power to make a real difference to children across the country.
This is a milestone worth celebrating and an investment in a healthier future for the next generation.
Sarah Orves, Headteacher of Ilketshall Lawrence Primary in Suffolk, said:
Lunchtimes used to be just a moment to refuel and get back to the day, but it was our pupils themselves who told us they wanted change.

We started the journey of transforming our school food a year ago, introducing ‘Try it Tuesday’ and family taster sessions to bring both children and families on board, and now lunchtimes are something the kids genuinely feel excited about.

We’re only halfway through that journey, but we’re already noticing the difference: children are more social and settled at lunch, more focused in class, and genuinely excited to try new foods and engage with being healthy.

To give parents greater confidence in school meals, schools will be expected to publish their food policies and menus online and nominate a school food governor, helping parents, pupils and communities understand and hold schools to account for the food on offer.

To help schools implement the new standards, the government will provide training, resources and guidance. The Department for Education will work with the Food Standards Agency on an approach to monitoring school food, with more details in the coming months.

Alongside the historic expansion of free school meals and the rollout of free breakfast clubs, these changes represent the most significant package of school food improvements in a generation, giving parents confidence that their child is receiving healthy, nutritious food throughout the school day and helping children focus, learn and succeed at school.
Additional Quotes:
Anna Taylor, Executive Director, The Food Foundation, said:

Today marks another massive step on the journey to improve children’s health across the country. Good school food standards are critical to making that happen and the School Food Project is there to help schools train up their kitchen teams and work with pupils to improve menus. This all needs to be underpinned by a robust approach to monitoring and supporting schools to improve.
Over the coming year, in the run-up to enforcement in September 2027, parents and children can expect to start seeing real improvements.
Every child deserves the best possible start in life - and that means school food that packs a nutritional punch while bringing genuine pleasure and wellbeing to every child’s mealtime.
Bite Back campaigner, Zainab (19), said:

I was in Year 10 when I joined Bite Back, and since then I’ve campaigned alongside other young people for better school food. Bite Back exists to make sure young people are heard on decisions affecting our health, so it means a lot to see the Government listening.
Thousands of young people shared their experiences and ideas because we all want the same thing: great food in every school that helps children feel good, focus and thrive.

This announcement is an important step. We now look forward to working with the Government, schools and our partners to introduce the new standards successfully, monitor their impact and make sure they lead to real change in every school canteen.
Stephanie Slater MBE, founder and Chief Executive of School Food Matters, says:

We’re in schools every day and see the power of a nutritious school meal. We want to see delicious and nutritious meals in every school so today marks an important step towards equity in the school food system.
New standards and a framework for monitoring the quality of the food on offer will bring about the change we want to see: great school food that supports every child to thrive, wherever they live.
Naomi Duncan, CEO, Chefs in Schools, said:

Today is a huge day for children and young people. For far too long, excellent school kitchens serving fresh, tasty food have been competing with those serving up cheap, nutritionally barren junk. Today the government has drawn a line in the sand and committed to not just improving standards, but ensuring every single school kitchen is held to them.

We warmly welcome this action. History shows us that introducing higher standards leads in the long term to increasing uptake, when schools and caterers work together. Now the onus is on those of us who feed children every day in school to make sure that becomes reality again.

We’ve launched the School Food Project to support schools and caterers with implementation of these new ambitions, to protect and increase uptake and help to unleash the dynamism and creativity that we know exists in every school kitchen. We have a year to prepare and we shouldn’t waste a minute of it.
Charlotte Stirling-Reed -The Baby & Child Nutritionist:
I’ve been waiting a long time to see big changes happening once again with our school food.
It’s been over ten years since the School Food Standards were properly looked at, and in that time we’ve learned so much more about what children need to grow, develop and concentrate at school.
This feels as if it could be a pivotal moment for children’s health and I’m fully behind having clearer, more specific guidance around what foods should and shouldn’t be offered at school.

What I like most about these new school food recommendations is that the level of change being proposed seems just the right level - ambitious enough to make a real difference, but realistic enough for schools and caterers to actually put into practice with a little support.

With more children than ever now relying on free school meals, what’s served at school has never mattered more, and I really hope parents and schools get behind these changes and help push them forward, because the benefits will be felt by this generation of children and the ones who come after.
Professor Susan Jebb, Chair of the Food Standards Agency (FSA) said:

The FSA welcomes the Department for Education’s commitment in the 10-year health plan to update the School Food Standards, and we fully support the ambition to ensure children can access healthier food in schools.

We want to see school food standards that are effective in practice, and schools appropriately supported to meet them. That’s why we’ve been working closely with DfE, offering our expertise on food regulation, assurance and the practical considerations involved in implementation.

Our aim is to help shape a future approach that is practical, proportionate and deliverable, and we look forward to continuing to work with DfE to ensure every school is offering pupils food that meets the nutritional standards.
Dr Helen Stewart, Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health (RCPCH), Officer for Health Improvement said:

Childhood nutrition has never been more important. Our State of Child Health report highlights rising rates of childhood obesity, particularly among children in the most deprived communities, who are more likely to rely on school meals.

These changes are a welcome and long-overdue step towards ensuring all children have access to healthier food throughout the school day, helping to establish healthy habits that can last a lifetime. They also demonstrate the value of close collaboration between the health and education sectors in improving outcomes for children and giving every child the best possible start in life.
Katharine Jenner, Executive Director, Obesity Health Alliance said:

This is a major and very welcome step towards giving every child the best start in life. With one in three children leaving primary school above a healthy weight, we cannot afford to ignore the important role that school food plays in shaping children’s diets and long-term health.
Cutting back foods high in sugar, salt and saturated fat, while putting more fruit and vegetables on the menu, will help make the healthier choice the easier choice for millions of children.

Good school food will play an important role in achieving the government’s ambition to become a more preventative state. The next step is making sure these standards are properly implemented and monitored, so that every child benefits, regardless of where they live or their family’s income.
Brad Pearce, National Chair of The School Food People said:

The School Food People welcomes the Government’s continued ambition to improve children’s nutrition through revised School Food Standards. Our members and their dedicated frontline teams want to provide children and young people with nutritious, exciting and freshly prepared food that they genuinely want to eat every school day.

As the new standards roll out, it is vital that we protect the strength and sustainability of the school food sector that will be responsible for delivering them. That means realistic funding, a practical and fully supported implementation plan, investment in the workforce and kitchens, and sufficient time for caterers and suppliers to adapt and reformulate products where necessary.

We must also keep a close eye on meal uptake. New revised mandatory school food standards, while very much welcome, can only actually improve children’s diets if pupils continue to choose school meals. We are absolutely committed to working with Government, schools, families and the wider sector to make these changes a success.
Dr Oosh Devalia OBE, BSPD President said:

BSPD warmly welcomes the Government’s overhaul of school food. Tooth decay remains the most common reason for children aged five to nine to be admitted to hospital in England, usually to have decayed teeth removed under general anaesthetic. Sugar is the main driver of that decay, and it is also a key contributor to childhood obesity, so cutting it from school meals is a win for children’s overall health as well as their teeth.

For many children, particularly in our most deprived communities where decay rates are highest, a school lunch may be the main meal of their day. Getting it right matters. Tooth decay is almost entirely preventable, and every child deserves a healthy mouth.

captures.title: New research ship to be built in Britain, boosting British shipbuilding and transforming UK ocean science
captures.date_review_note: Official Content API explicitly records first publication.
captures.rights: GOV.UK内容一般适用Open Government Licence v3.0，须署名，且不覆盖徽标、个人信息及第三方权利；当前候选须逐篇排除第三方引文和媒体后才能公开分发。
captures.text:
A new government funded research ship, built in UK shipyards, will create jobs and help protect the nation’s climate, energy and food security. The government has committed to build this new vessel as part of its drive to reindustrialise the UK and support our shipyards.

The new ship will lead a new national system for monitoring the UK’s seas. It will bring together marine surveys, data and technology in one place, helping the nation manage fisheries and the marine environment more effectively.

At 85 metres long and able to accommodate more than 40 people, the vessel will carry out a wide range of scientific work. This includes assessing fish stocks, mapping the seabed, monitoring pollution, and responding quickly to marine incidents. It will use the latest technology, including automation, robotics and artificial intelligence, and will run on clean fuels, helping position the UK as a global leader in marine science while reducing environmental impact.

The UK’s seas contributed more than £200 billion to the economy in 2021. This investment reflects how important the marine environment is to the UK’s economy, security and long-term resilience.

The vessel will replace the RV Cefas Endeavour, which has supported UK marine science since 2003 and is due to retire in the early 2030s.

Defra Chief Scientific Adviser Professor Anjali Goswami said:

Science leadership and innovation are critical to informing the complex decision making necessary to balance the needs of people and nature, within a challenging context of economic, societal and environmental pressures.

By investing in a next-generation Research Vessel, we can continue to harness marine scientific understanding to make better decisions to safeguard our essential human needs: water, food and energy security.

Cefas CEO, Tim Green, said:

This once-in-a-generation investment is a significant moment for Cefas and UK marine science. This new vessel will give our scientists the capability to monitor and understand our changing seas, support sustainable fisheries and inform management decisions, and respond to growing marine challenges.

For 125 years, Cefas has worked alongside coastal communities and the fishing industry from our main sites in Lowestoft and Weymouth to deliver world-leading marine science.

This investment will build on that proud heritage, create opportunities for the next generation and ensure that they have the tools to shape the future of our seas.

The new vessel is expected to be operational in 2031 or 2032, continuing over 125-years of world-leading UK marine research. Delivery of the vessel will be led by the Centre for Environment, Fisheries and Aquaculture Science (Cefas), which has laboratories in Lowestoft and Weymouth.

The government expects to engage with the UK shipbuilding sector in the coming months to plan the next stage of the procurement process. The vessel’s design will reflect the specialist scientific needs of the mission.

captures.title: Chancellor announces Bank of England appointments
captures.date_review_note: Official Content API explicitly records first publication.
captures.rights: GOV.UK内容一般适用Open Government Licence v3.0，须署名，且不覆盖徽标、个人信息及第三方权利；当前候选须逐篇排除第三方引文和媒体后才能公开分发。
captures.text:
David Craig and Paul Nowak are appointed to four-year terms until 31 August 2030. Hanneke Smits will begin her four-year term on 1 January 2027, until 31 December 2030.

David Craig and Paul Nowak take up the positions vacated by Sir Ron Kalifa and Baroness Frances O’Grady. David Craig and Paul Nowak will attend their first Court meetings on 17 September and 22 October respectively. Hanneke Smits will take up the position currently held by Sabine Chalmers, who has informed the Court of her intention to resign her role at the end of October 2026, and Hanneke Smits will attend her first Court meeting on 11 February 2027.

These new appointments come alongside the reappointment of Lord Jitesh Gadhia and Tom Shropshire as non-executive directors for a second four-year team. Lord Jitesh Gadhia will begin his four-year term on the 24 October 2026, and Tom Shropshire will begin his four-year term on the 1 November 2026.

Chancellor of the Exchequer, John Healey, said:

These appointments strengthen the Court at a critical moment for the UK economy, providing deep and varied experience to support the Bank in delivering its core missions of monetary and financial stability.

David Roberts, Chair of Court, said:

The Governor and I wish to thank Sabine Chalmers for her dedication to the Bank of England over the past four years and the insights she has brought to the Court throughout that time, including her support for the Bank’s culture and people development agenda.

On behalf of Court, I am delighted to welcome David, Paul and Hanneke, who bring considerable insight and experience that will aid the Court in executing on our responsibilities. I look forward to continuing working with Jitesh and Tom following their reappointment, as we continue to drive forward the changes needed to ensure the Bank is well placed to deliver in the coming years.

Paul Nowak is General Secretary of the Trades Union Congress. The TUC represents 47 unions and 5.3 million workers in the UK. Paul has represented the TUC internationally at the International Labour Organisation, OECD and G20, and holds non-executive experience at Unity Trust Bank.

David Craig is a senior financial markets and data technology executive with over 30 years’ leadership experience. He founded and led Refinitiv as CEO, building it into a global leader in financial data, technology and trading platforms before instigating its acquisition by London Stock Exchange Group, where he subsequently led the Data and Analytics Division. Amongst other financial industry technology and data roles, he co-chairs the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures.

Hanneke Smits is a senior investment management executive with 34 years’ experience, including as former Global Head of BNY Investment Management and a member of BNY’s Executive Committee. Whilst at BNY Hanneke also served on a few subsidiary asset management boards (Alcentra, Insight, Newton and Walter Scott). She has previously served on the Court and brings extensive non-executive experience across the Wellcome Trust, the Van Leer Foundation and the Education Endowment Foundation.

Lord Gadhia has over 25 years’ investment banking and financial services experience, having held senior positions at Blackstone, Barclays Capital, ABN AMRO and Baring Brothers. He currently serves on the boards of Rolls-Royce Holdings plc and Taylor Wimpey plc, and previously served on the boards of UK Financial Investments Limited and UK Government Investments Limited from 2014 to 2022. He has been a member of the House of Lords since 2016. He is also Chair of The British Asian Trust, a charitable foundation established by His Majesty King Charles III.

Tom Shropshire is Senior Vice President and General Counsel of Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. Prior to this, he was General Counsel and Company Secretary of Diageo plc. Before joining Diageo, he was a partner at Linklaters LLP, where he was Global Head of US Practice and co-head of the Risk and Resilience Practice. He is a trustee of the New York University School of Law and a former trustee and chair of Comic Relief.

The Court of the Bank of England acts as the Bank’s board. It is responsible for overseeing the Bank’s strategy, governance, budget and risk framework, and for ensuring the effective discharge of the Bank’s statutory functions.

The Court consists of the Chair and eight other Non-Executive Directors, the Governor and four Deputy Governors. Non-Executive Directors bring independent judgement and a breadth of experience to the Court’s deliberations.

The appointment followed a fair and open competition in line with the Governance Code on Public Appointments.

Appointments and reappointments to the Court of the Bank of England are not automatic. Each case is considered on its own merits.

David Craig, Paul Nowak, Hanneke Smits, Lord Jitesh Gadhia and Tom Shropshire have confirmed that they have not engaged in any significant party political activity in the last five years.

captures.title: Over £1.5 billion to help NHS withstand year-round pressure
captures.date_review_note: Official Content API explicitly records first publication.
captures.rights: GOV.UK内容一般适用Open Government Licence v3.0，须署名，且不覆盖徽标、个人信息及第三方权利；当前候选须逐篇排除第三方引文和媒体后才能公开分发。
captures.text:
Over £200 million for 10 major projects, including new operating theatres, children’s wards and improved maternity and mental health facilities

£1.3 billion for maintenance, safety and resilience projects across the NHS estate, including £32 million for specific projects that are improving cooling and ventilation systems and strengthening hospitals’ resilience to extreme heat

Investment will help hospitals prepare for winter and extreme weather, and protect capacity to help alleviate pressures on the health sector

Patients across England will benefit from safer and more resilient NHS hospitals thanks to over £1.5 billion of investment to tackle urgent problems with hospital buildings and facilities.

Over £200 million will fund 10 major hospital projects, while over £1.3 billion will go towards maintenance, safety and resilience improvements.

The investment comes as the NHS adapts to increasing year-round pressures. For decades, hospitals have focused on preparing for winter demand, but periods of extreme heat and sustained pressure on services mean the NHS must be equipped for new challenges. This investment will help hospitals remain safe, open and able to care for patients throughout the year.

The government has announced that this will include more than £200 million for 10 major projects across the country, helping patients receive care in safer, better-equipped facilities.

The investment will fund improvements including:

new operating theatres

a new ward for children

safer maternity and mental health facilities

improvements to protect vital services that help doctors diagnose and treat patients

Alongside action being taken to improve urgent and emergency care, the investment will also strengthen the long-term resilience of NHS services by addressing ageing infrastructure and critical safety risks across the estate. It will help hospitals cope with changing patterns of demand while maintaining safe, high-quality care for patients.

The investment will also support wider efforts to improve patient flow through hospitals, complementing ongoing work with community and social care services to help patients receive the right care in the right place and leave hospital safely when they are ready.

It is part of a wider programme of more than 950 projects across the NHS, targeting the hospitals and facilities most in need of investment and helping them stay safe and open for patients, including during periods of high pressure over winter.

Yvette Cooper, Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, said:

For decades, hospitals have focused on preparing for winter pressures, but the NHS is now facing new challenges, including periods of extreme heat and sustained pressure on services throughout the year.

That’s why we are investing more than £1.5 billion to make our NHS hospitals safer and more resilient, helping them remain open and able to care for patients when pressure on services is greatest.

This includes investment in cooling and ventilation systems to help hospitals adapt to more frequent periods of extreme heat, alongside hundreds of projects to tackle urgent safety and infrastructure risks across the NHS estate.

This is just the start. Through our 10 Year Capital Plan , we will continue investing in the NHS buildings and facilities staff and patients need, helping build a health service that is fit for the future.

The over £200 million investment will deliver major improvements for patients across England, including:

Stepping Hill Hospital, Stockport - £26 million: a new pathology building will protect the testing services doctors rely on to diagnose patients and provide urgent care

Bristol Royal Infirmary, Bristol - £41 million: improvements to operating theatres will make the facilities safer and more reliable for patients needing surgery

Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Gateshead - £12 million: redevelopment of maternity facilities will provide a better environment for women receiving care

Wycombe Hospital, Buckinghamshire - £25 million: a new clinical building will allow services to move out of an ageing tower and into modern facilities

Crystal Centre and Linden Centre, Essex - £15 million: 14 new bedrooms will provide additional space for mental health patients and allow existing wards to be improved

Lister Hospital, Hertfordshire - £11 million: a new children’s ward will provide safe, modern space for children needing hospital care

Southend Hospital, Essex - £1 million: planning will begin to replace an ageing hospital tower, helping provide safer facilities for maternity, neonatal, cancer and outpatient care

St George’s Hospital, Stafford - £25 million: improvements to a mental health unit will replace ageing facilities and provide a safer environment for patients

Royal Free Hospital, London - £32 million: 2 new operating theatres will give patients access to safer, modern facilities for complex operations

John Howard Centre, London - £25 million: refurbishment will create safer, more suitable facilities for people receiving long-term mental health care

Alongside the 10 major projects, more than 950 schemes have been approved across the country. These projects will fix urgent problems that can affect patients and staff - from improving fire safety and replacing old ventilation systems to upgrading electrical equipment.

This includes more than £32 million for projects that involve improving cooling, ventilation and overheating, helping hospitals adapt to more frequent periods of extreme heat and reducing the risk of disruption to patient care. These include:

Manchester Royal Infirmary - £154,000 to replace the PET scanner chiller, ensuring reliable temperature control for highly sensitive imaging

Rampton Hospital, Nottinghamshire - £527,000 to replace air conditioning in a unit, keeping areas cool to maintain a stable environment for patients, staff and visitors

St Peter’s Hospital, Ashford - £791,000 to restore reliable cooling capacity to support safe operating conditions within theatres

The improvements will help to:

maintain safe temperatures for patients and staff

protect critical equipment

improve the resilience of hospital services during heatwaves

As part of improving overall estate safety and planning for next summer, the Secretary of State has instructed the NHS to look at heatwaves and other necessary safety schemes - such as increasing resilience to flooding - in the next round, drawing on their experience from this summer.

The investment comes as the NHS prepares for winter and follows a summer of significant pressure on health services. Tackling problems that can disrupt care, including those caused by extreme temperatures and ageing infrastructure, will help NHS staff provide treatment in safe, reliable facilities when demand is at its highest.

It is backed by a record capital budget for health, rising to £15 billion in 2029 to 2030, and the government’s 10 Year Capital Plan, which will put NHS investment on a long-term footing and rebuild and modernise the health service for patients.

Sir Ciarán Devane, Chief Executive of the NHS Alliance, said:

We welcome this investment. The summer heatwaves showed up the poor condition of many NHS buildings which are dilapidated and poorly designed to cope with hot weather.

This funding will help both staff and patient wellbeing. All efforts to improve productivity are a good thing though the context is that the NHS continues to face a sizeable maintenance backlog, including a number of issues that require prompt action to address.

Background information

Investment is from the £6.75 billion Estates Safety Fund, part of the government’s record capital budget for health.

These schemes have been proposed and prioritised by the NHS locally within their Estates Scheme Fund funding allocations, in line with the process set out in the NHS capital planning guidance .

See the full list of projects: Estates Safety Fund: initial schemes and associated funding allocations, 2026 to 2030 .

This list represents an initial set of projects approved to proceed to detailed design stage. More schemes will be confirmed in future as NHS investment plans are finalised.

Final scheme cost and scope will be subject to future business case approvals.

£1.3 billion for maintenance, safety and resilience projects across the NHS estate, including £32 million for specific projects that are improving cooling and ventilation systems and strengthening hospitals’ resilience to extreme heat
Investment will help hospitals prepare for winter and extreme weather, and protect capacity to help alleviate pressures on the health sector
Patients across England will benefit from safer and more resilient NHS hospitals thanks to over £1.5 billion of investment to tackle urgent problems with hospital buildings and facilities.
Over £200 million will fund 10 major hospital projects, while over £1.3 billion will go towards maintenance, safety and resilience improvements.

new operating theatres
a new ward for children
safer maternity and mental health facilities
improvements to protect vital services that help doctors diagnose and treat patients
